slides.title: Announcements
items: Mid-course survey — group work and pacing.
A quick note on malloc() in embedded code.
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 90 s — trimmed to buy Part 6 its block diagram. The malloc aside is ES 20 continuity, not ADC content: embedded code allocates statically; a heap you cannot inspect on a part with 12 KB of RAM is a liability. One sentence, then move on.

slides.title: What the Number Means
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 5 min. The reading already did this arithmetic — this is retrieval. If more than a few hands are still empty after the prediction, the reading did not land: spend the full 5 and work 1.65 V out loud on the board.

slides.title: Which Pins Can Do Analog?
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 9 min. Budget 2–3 min just to get 30 people onto the right page of the right PDF. Datasheet Table 12 — the day's datasheet moment.

slides.title: CHSELR — bit n selects channel n
The Test Circuit
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 10 min, and this is the part most likely to overrun. Pots are NOT pre-seated: students either push the pins hard into the breadboard or use three pin-to-clip jumpers. Budget the full 10 and watch for the wiper going to an outer leg.

slides.title: The Registers, One at a Time
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 6 min. Open with the analogRead slide so the registers do not arrive from nowhere, then one register per slide. TODOs 1 and 3 are shown on PA4 / channel 4 — theirs is PA0 / channel 0, so those are transfer. TODOs 4 and 5 need this slide's shape plus the ADC_ISR bit names. TODO 2 is one invariant line.

slides.title: What analogRead() was doing for you
Waiting for a flag — you know this one
Writing ADCPot.c
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 20 min. THE CRUCIAL STEP — never cut this. Leave the diagnostic slide up for the whole part, and hand out the half-sheet version.

slides.title: Make the knob move the number
Finished early?
slides.body: Turn the knob to each mechanical end stop. Do you read exactly 0 and exactly 4095? If not — is the explanation in the potentiometer, or in the converter?
slides.presenterNote: The 2-minute stretch. The two big stretches are homework — say so, don't start them in class. ANSWER: two causes. The pot's mechanical stops leave a little track resistance at each end, and the converter itself has an offset error because we never calibrated it — Lab 4's ADVREGEN/ADCAL sequence is what removes the second half.

slides.title: Wait — How Did That Clear the Bit?
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 7 min. The day's set-piece. If you must cut, cut it WHOLE — never truncate it. An unanswered puzzle is worse than one never raised.

slides.title: Successive Approximation, Live
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 4 min, compressible to 2 as a whole-class call-and-response. Block diagram and timing are in the book's Reference section — do not re-teach them here; the reading already has them.

slides.title: Today, and where it goes
items: A count is a number of steps: V = count × 3.3 / 4096.
The datasheet says which pins do analog, and on which channel.
Configure once; then start, wait, read — every sample.
Status registers clear by writing 1, because two parties write them.
One comparison per bit is why a conversion takes ~14 clocks.
Lab 4 starts exactly where tonight's homework ends.
